name: Vadhavan Port (greenfield major port, artificial island)
agency: Vadhavan Port Project Ltd (VPPL) — SPV of Jawaharlal Nehru Port Authority (74%) and Maharashtra Maritime Board (26%); VPPL incorporated 14 September 2016
operational_consequences: Designed as India's first offshore port; the deepest-draft capacity addition of the programme, aimed at ultra-large container vessels that currently bypass Indian gateways.

name: Vizhinjam International Seaport, Phase 1 (deepwater transshipment port)
agency: Vizhinjam International Seaport Ltd (Kerala government) with Adani Ports & SEZ as concessionaire
operational_consequences: Keeps Indian-bound transshipment cargo in Indian terminals instead of Colombo/Dubai/Singapore; anchor for a port-adjacent services economy in Thiruvananthapuram.

name: Road over bridge at level crossing LC-235, Deendayal Port
operational_consequences: Port-gate works like this affect node logistics for port-linked industry (including the Sanand semiconductor node served by Deendayal) without ever naming the node.

name: Obulavaripalle–Venkatachalam (Krishnapatnam) new rail line
cost_note: Cost not captured from a primary source; SDCL's ₹125 crore equity contribution into KRCL is documented.
agency: Krishnapatnam Railway Company Ltd (KRCL) with Sagarmala Development Company Ltd equity
operational_consequences: Rail evacuation capacity for one of the largest private ports on the east coast; enables bulk exports (iron ore, coal) and container movement between the hinterland and the port.

name: Haridaspur–Paradip rail line and doubling
status_note: New line completed; doubling under implementation per the February 2026 Odisha connectivity reply.
cost_note: ₹2,542 crore is the doubling cost; the original new line estimate was ₹1,365 crore. HPRCL authorised capital is ₹1,500 crore with SDCL holding 25.91%.
agency: Haridaspur Paradip Railway Company Ltd (HPRCL) with Sagarmala Development Company Ltd equity (₹33.68 crore = 25.91%)
operational_consequences: Raises rail evacuation throughput for Paradip's dry-bulk and cargo flows; a listed bottleneck-removal project for the Odisha port cluster.

name: Jal Marg Vikas Project — NW-1 multimodal terminals
operational_consequences: Adds a water leg for bulk and container movement in the Gangetic hinterland; NW-1 carries ~4 million tonnes, growing from a near-zero base.

name: NW-2, NW-3 and NW-4 terminal programme
location: Brahmaputra (NW-2), West Coast Canal Kerala (NW-3), Kakinada–Puducherry canals/Godavari (NW-4)
cost_note: Individual terminal costs not published in captured sources.
operational_consequences: Extends waterway freight and passenger capacity beyond the Ganga corridor; NW-2 carries ~2 million tonnes and NW-3 ~1 million tonne.

name: NW-5 Phase-1 (Talcher–Dhamra–Paradip–Pankapal)
cost_note: Cost not published in captured sources.
operational_consequences: Potential modal shift for thermal coal and minerals from road to water in Odisha's mining belt.

name: Ghogha–Hazira Ro-Pax ferry service
status_note: Hazira Ro-Pax facility completed in CY2023; vessels have moved ~36,000 trucks, 61,000 cars and ~4 lakh passengers.
cost_note: Individual cost not isolated from the 29-project Ro-Pax package (₹1,233 crore).
agency: Gujarat Maritime Board with MoPSW support
operational_consequences: Removes a coastal-road leg for Saurashtra truck traffic and anchors the Ghogha coastal cluster.

name: Coastal berth programme
location: Multiple states (Visakhapatnam, JNPT, Kollam, Old Mangaluru, VOCPT among others)
status_note: Seven berths completed; more sanctioned in the 128-project scheme list (Visakhapatnam coastal berth completed 30/09/2017 at ₹43 crore; JNPT, Kollam, Old Mangaluru and VOCPT berths in the list).
agency: Respective port authorities with MoPSW financial assistance
operational_consequences: Dedicated coastal berths lower the cost and dwell of coastal transshipment, the policy basis for raising coastal shipping's modal share.

name: Fishing harbour and fish landing centre programme
location: Multiple coastal states (Malpe and Kulai in Karnataka; Juvvaladinne and Visakhapatnam in AP; Chennai, Mookaiyur, Kunthukal, Poompuhar and Chinnamuttom in Tamil Nadu; Cochin, Thalai, Chettuva and Chellanam in Kerala; Sassoon Dock, Mallet Bunder, Karanja, Anandwadi, Mirkawada in Maharashtra; Mangrol in Gujarat; Paradip and Chandipur in Odisha)
status_note: 11 completed; several others under implementation in the 128-project scheme list.
agency: Port authorities, state maritime boards and state fisheries departments
operational_consequences: Landing-centre infrastructure is the base of the coastal cold chain; its industrial relevance depends on downstream cold-storage and processing investment.

name: Centre of Excellence in Maritime and Shipbuilding (CEMS)
agency: Indian Register of Shipping with MoPSW support
operational_consequences: Training capacity for shipbuilding-adjacent trades; the only scheme-funded skills asset of scale captured so far.

name: Lighthouse tourism programme
location: Nationwide (Directorate General of Lighthouses and Lightships)
cost_note: Programme cost not published in captured sources.
agency: Directorate General of Lighthouses and Lightships (MoPSW)
operational_consequences: Coastal-tourism infrastructure with local employment effects that are not independently measured on file.
